<document>
<title>Doraemon</title>
<fragment>
*Doraemon* is considered one of the best-known manga of all time, a true Japanese cultural icon,[10] and an essential part of family life of the Japanese post-war generation.[152] Akihiro Motoyama observed that "mothers who watched the movies when they were children are now taking their own children to see them".[152][174] It was also commercially successful: over 108 million books were sold in Japan by 1996.[175] The 1979[174] and 2005 anime series[176] also achieved high ratings on television. With the film *Doraemon: Nobita's Secret Gadget Museum*, the *Doraemon* anime film series reached 100 million tickets sold at the Japanese box office, surpassing *Godzilla* as the highest-grossing film franchise in Japan.[177] By 2015, it had sold over 103 million tickets, and was the largest franchise by numbers of admissions in the country.[178]


</fragment>

<fragment>

A 2006 poll among 80,000 Japanese fans for the 10th anniversary of the Japan Media Arts Festival placed *Doraemon* at fifth among the top ten best manga of all time.[216] The 2005 and 2006 surveys conducted by TV Asahi found the *Doraemon* anime ranked fifth and third, respectively, among the 100 most favorite anime series of all time.[217][218] In 2010, a survey conducted by researchers of Tokyo Polytechnic University found that most responders considered *Doraemon*, along with *Dragon Ball* franchise, to be the anime series that represents Cool Japan.[219] In a 2013 survey, *Doraemon* was found to be the best anime recommended for foreign people.[220]



### Controversies

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>

*Doraemon* was also a hit in Asia in general, and was considered one of the typical cases of Japanese soft power,[179] although it was published without a license in some countries.[180] The anime television series is available in over 60 countries,[93] and reportedly getting high ratings in at least 30 countries.[181] However, *Doraemon* was less successful in Western countries, because it was viewed as a children-only series, and there were some tight restrictions about publishing manga and broadcasting anime series there.[182][183] The manga has sold over 170 million copies worldwide by 2012,[184][185] and 250 million by 2019.[186] Estimates show that *Doraemon* has generated at least more than $4.3 billion in merchandise sales by 2019,[a] and over $1.7 billion from anime feature films by 2020,[197] making it one of the highest-grossing media franchises of all time.


</fragment>

Based on my research from Wikipedia articles, here's a summary of the popularity and acclaim of these five major anime protagonists:

## **Goku (Dragon Ball)**
- **Top Rankings:** Ranked #1 in IGN's 2009 list of Top 25 Anime Characters of All Time, and #3 in their 2014 updated list
- **Fan Polls:** Won first place in Weekly Shōnen Jump's 1995 popularity poll and ranked first among fans in Dragon Ball Forever (2004)
- **Historical Recognition:** Voted the "Strongest Manga character of all time" in a 2007 Oricon survey of 1,000 people
- **Cultural Impact:** Described as revolutionizing shōnen manga and being a character that "bucked the trends of his time and defined the direction of shōnen manga/anime for decades"

## **Naruto Uzumaki (Naruto)**
- **Shōnen Jump Polls:** Consistently ranked in the top five characters in every official Weekly Shōnen Jump popularity poll, achieving first place multiple times including 2011 and 2012
- **IGN Recognition:** Ranked #2 best Naruto character by IGN when the series ended
- **Japanese Rankings:** Voted 13th "strongest hero" from the Heisei Era in a 2017 Japanese TV special
- **Historical Significance:** Voted 10th most powerful character in Shōnen Jump's 50-year history in a 2018 poll
- **Political Recognition:** Ranked 9th most ideal Prime Minister in anime series in a 2017 Charapedia poll

## **Eren Yeager (Attack on Titan)**
- **Newtype Awards:** Voted 8th best male character in the 3rd Newtype Anime Awards (2013) and 10th most popular male anime character from the 2010s
- **Animage Ranking:** Ranked 4th most popular male anime character in Anime Grand Prix 2014 polls
- **Recent Awards:** Won Best Antagonist at the 6th Crunchyroll Anime Awards while being nominated for Best Protagonist and Best Fight Scene
- **Character Recognition:** Won the "Hot" award in Animedia character awards and appeared in Newtype polls as recently as July 2021

## **Edward Elric (Fullmetal Alchemist)**
- **Manga Polls:** Consistently ranked first in Monthly Shōnen Gangan popularity polls
- **Award Recognition:** Won the Twenty-sixth Annual Animage Readers' Poll for "Favorite Male Character"
- **IGN Ranking:** Placed 7th on IGN's 2009 Top 25 Anime Characters of All Time list
- **Newtype Rankings:** Ranked first in Male Character Rankings in July 2009 Newtype issue, and 4th most popular male anime character from the 2000s in March 2010
- **About.com Award:** Won "Best Lead Character – Male" in Anime Awards 2006

## **Monkey D. Luffy (One Piece)**
- **Global Popularity:** Ranked first in ALL One Piece Characters Official Popularity Polls, one of only two main protagonists to achieve this feat
- **Historical Achievement:** Topped the 1st Global One Piece Characters Popularity Poll with over 1.6 million votes from more than 12 million global voters
- **IGN Ranking:** Placed 22nd on Chris Mackenzie's IGN list of top-25 anime characters of all time
- **Japanese Recognition:** Voted 8th "strongest hero" from the Showa Era and 4th from the Heisei Era in a 2017 Japanese TV special
- **Cultural Impact:** His Gum-Gum Gatling technique topped surveys of most popular moves in manga and anime

**Summary:** All five protagonists are highly acclaimed, with Goku and Luffy showing particularly strong global recognition, while Edward Elric and Naruto demonstrate remarkable consistency in fan polls, and Eren Yeager represents more recent critical acclaim, especially for his complex character evolution in Attack on Titan.

*Dragon Ball* has become one of the most successful manga series of all time. Its initial serialization in *Weekly Shōnen Jump* was partly responsible for the magazine reaching its highest circulation of 6.53 million weekly sales. Its collected *tankōbon* volumes have over 160 million copies sold in Japan and 260 million sold worldwide,[2][a][c] making it one of the best-selling manga series. Reviewers have praised the manga for its comedy, fight scenes, and pacing, while recognizing a coming-of-age theme and its use of cultural references from Chinese mythology and Japanese folktales. Complaints from parents in the United States resulted in English-language releases being edited to remove nudity, racial stereotypes, and other content.

*One Piece* was the best-selling manga series for eleven consecutive years from 2008 until 2018.[130] In 2019, the manga did not top the chart for the first time in twelve years, ranking second in the annual manga sales ranking with over 10.1 million copies sold,[131] although it remained as the best-selling manga by volume in its twelfth consecutive year.[132] It was the third best-selling manga series in 2020, with over 7.7 million copies sold,[133] while volumes 95–97 were the 23rd–25th best-selling manga volumes of 2020, behind the first twenty-two volumes of *Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba*.[134] In 2021, it was the sixth best selling manga with over 7 million copies sold,[135] while volumes 98, 99, and 100 were the sixth, eighth, and ninth best-selling manga volumes, respectively.[136] It was the fourth best-selling manga series in 2022, 
</fragment>

*One Piece* is the best-selling manga series in history; in 2012, Oricon, a Japanese company that began its own annual manga sales ranking chart in year 2008, reported that the series was the first to sell 100 million copies (the company does not report on sales figures before April 2008).[116] The series had over 300 million copies in circulation by November 2013;[117] it had over 440 million copies in circulation worldwide by May 2018;[118] 460 million copies by December 2019;[119][120] 470 million copies by April 2020;[121][122] 480 million copies in circulation in forty-three countries worldwide by February 2021.[123][124] It reached 490 million copies in print worldwide by July 2021.[125][126] By August 2022, the manga had reached 516,566,000 copies in circulation worldwide.[127][128][129]

msg.content:
<document>
<title>Oricon</title>
<fragment>
Oricon monitors and reports on sales of CDs, DVDs, video games, and entertainment content in several other formats; manga and book sales were also formerly covered. Charts are published every Tuesday in *Oricon Style* and on Oricon's official website. Every Monday, Oricon receives data from outlets, but data on merchandise sold through certain channels does not make it into the charts. For example, the debut single of NEWS, a pop group, was released only through 7-Eleven stores, which are not covered by Oricon, and its sales were not reflected in the Oricon charts. Oricon's rankings of record sales are therefore not completely accurate. Before data was collected electronically, the charts were compiled on the basis of faxes that were sent from record shops.



## Controversy

[edit]

</document>

Based on my search of Wikipedia articles and manga sales data, here's an analysis of manga circulation milestones and recent series that achieved impressive sales:

## Major Manga Circulation Thresholds

### 100+ Million Copies - The Elite Tier:
- **One Piece**: ~516.6 million tankōbon volumes available (not counting individual chapter sales)
- **Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba**: Achieved over 150 million copies in circulation
- **Dragon Ball**: Over 260 million copies worldwide
- **Slam Dunk**: Notable resurgence with sales reaching several tens of millions

### Notable Recent Milestones Achieved:

**Blue Lock** - Football manga that showed remarkable growth:
- August 2020: 1.9 million copies
- January 2021: 3 million copies  
- April 2021: 4 million copies
- August 2021: 5 million copies
- February 2022: 6 million copies
- March 2022: 8.3 million copies
- June 2022: 9.3 million copies
- August 2022: 10 million copies (first major milestone)
- December 2022: 16 million copies
- January 2023: 18 million copies
- February 2023: 21.5 million copies
- March 2023: 24 million copies
- April 2023: 25.5 million copies
- May 2023: 26 million copies
- July 2023: 27 million copies
- August 2023: 28 million copies

**Tokyo Revengers**:
- 2021: Third best-selling manga with over 24.9 million copies sold
- 2022: Second best-selling with over 11 million copies sold

**Spy × Family**:
- By 2021: Had already sold over 10 million copies before anime adaptation
- Continued strong performance through 2022, topping manga rankings

**Kaiju No. 8**:
- Noted as the "Fastest Shonen Jump Plus Manga to Reach 1 Million Copies in Print"
- By June 2021: Already at 2.5 million copies with just 3 volumes
- By February 2023: Over 400 million total views online

## Key Observations:

1. **Speed vs. Longevity**: Series like Blue Lock and Kaiju No. 8 achieved rapid milestones in short periods, while classics like One Piece accumulated sales over decades.

2. **20-30 Million Club**: Many successful modern manga series reach this tier, including Blue Lock (28 million), Chihayafuru (28 million), and others.

3. **Anime Impact**: Both Spy × Family and Demon Slayer saw significant sales boosts following anime adaptations.

4. **Digital-First Success**: Kaiju No. 8's online-first approach demonstrated the viability of digital-first manga in today's market.

The most impressive recent milestones are Blue Lock's trajectory from under 2 million to 28 million copies in just 3 years, and Kaiju No. 8's rapid digital and print success in the competitive Shonen Jump Plus market.

*Tokyo Revengers* was the third best-selling manga series in the first half of 2021 with over 5 million copies sold.[195] It was the third best-selling manga in 2021, with over 24.9 million copies sold.[196] It was the second best-selling manga series in 2022, with over 11 million copies sold;[197] volumes 25–29 were among the 25 best-selling manga volumes of the year.[198]



### Anime

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>
*Tokyo Revengers* won the 44th Kodansha Manga Award in the *shōnen* category in 2020.[180][181][182] The series ranked ninth on the 2021 "Book of the Year" list by *Da Vinci* magazine;[183] it ranked eighteenth on the 2022 list.[184] It ranked twelfth on Takarajimasha's *Kono Manga ga Sugoi!* 2022 list of best manga for male readers.[185]



#### Sales

[edit]

By February 2020, the manga had over 3 million copies in circulation;[186] it had over 17 million copies in circulation by May 2021;[187] over 20 million copies in circulation by June 2021;[188] over 25 million copies in circulation by July 2021;[189] over 35 million copies in circulation by August 2021;[190] over 40 million copies in circulation by September 2021;[191] over 50 million copies in circulation by January 2022;[192] over 65 million copies in circulation by July 2022, including 7 million copies outside of Japan;[193] and over 70 million copies in circulation by December 2022.[194]

* Demon Slayer (shogi), a trap opening in shogi
* *Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba*, a manga and anime series
	+ *Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba – The Movie: Mugen Train*, a 2020 anime film
	+ *Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba – The Hinokami Chronicles*, a 2021 video game
	+ *Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba – To the Swordsmith Village*, a 2023 anime film
	+ Demon Slayer Corps, a fictional organization
* Demon Slayers, fictional families in the manga and anime series *Omamori Himari*
* Demon Slayers, a fictional clan formed by Sango, Kohaku, and other characters in the manga and anime series *Inuyasha*
* Demon-Slayer Sword, a fictional sword used by Asta in the manga and anime series *Black Clover*
* The main character in this anime are the brother and sister name tanjiro and nezuko.
* *Megami Tensei Gaiden: Last Bible*, also titled *Revelations: The Demon Slayer*, a 1992 video game

Based on my search of Wikipedia articles for major modern manga series, I can provide you with detailed sales data for some of the best-selling manga, particularly focusing on recent years where "Attack on Titan" has achieved remarkable success. Here's what I found:

## **Attack on Titan Sales Performance**

**Record-Breaking Achievements:**
- In 2014, Attack on Titan actually **topped One Piece in half-year sales**, a significant achievement given One Piece's typically dominant position
- The manga broke records with what was certified as the "largest comic book ever published" by Guinness World Records
- by May 2021, it had achieved tremendous sales milestones

**Strong Performance Across Multiple Years:**
- Consistently appeared in top-selling manga rankings throughout 2013-2021
- Ranked high in "Kono Manga ga Sugoi" reader polls
- Topped Da Vinci Magazine's manga rankings for 2 consecutive years

## **Comparison with Other Major Series**

**Demon Slayer (Kimetsu no Yaiba):**
- Had explosive growth, becoming the #1 selling manga in 2020
- One volume sold a record 5.17 million copies in 2021
- Was the 2nd highest-selling manga after One Piece in 2019
- Overtook One Piece for the top position in recent years

**One Piece:**
- Traditionally dominated sales charts for years
- Volume 105 sold 1.76 million copies in 2023 (1st half)
- Maintains strong consistent performance year after year

**Jujutsu Kaisen:**
- Had massive growth from 2020-2023
- Reached 80 million copies in circulation by July 2023
- Became the top-selling manga series in 2022, edging out Tokyo Revengers
- Volume 18 sold 2.11 million copies in 2022

**My Hero Academia:**
- Consistent performer in top rankings
- Regular appearance in year-end bestseller lists
- Strong international and domestic sales

## **Key Takeaways:**

1. **Attack on Titan's peak performance** around 2013-2014 was exceptional, even briefly surpassing One Piece
2. **Demon Slayer** became the phenomenon that truly challenged One Piece's dominance in 2020-2021
3. **Jujutsu Kaisen** emerged as another major success, taking the #1 spot in 2022
4. The manga market has seen more competition at the top in recent years rather than One Piece's previous uncontested dominance

The data suggests that while Attack on Titan had its moment breaking records and challenging top series, the period around 2020-2022 saw the most competitive landscape with Demon Slayer and Jujutsu Kaisen achieving unprecedented success levels that even surpassed Attack on Titan's peak years.

Based on my search through Wikipedia articles and related sources, I can provide you with the most recent One Piece sales data that's available, though I must note that the specific 2023-2024 data you're looking for appears to be limited in the Wikipedia sources I could access.

## Key Findings from Wikipedia Sources:

### Current Total Circulation Numbers:
- **516.6 million copies** worldwide (as listed in the "List of best-selling manga" article)
- This includes both print and digital sales
- This appears to be from August 2022 when One Piece set a Guinness World Record for surpassing 500 million copies published

### Recent Milestones Found:

**July 2021:** One Piece surpassed **490 million** copies in circulation worldwide
   - Over 400 million in Japan
   - 90 million in at least 57 countries and regions overseas

**August 2022:** One Piece set **Guinness World Record** for surpassing **500 million** copies published worldwide
   - 416,566,000 copies in Japan
   - 100 million copies in 60 countries and territories outside of Japan

### Volume-Specific Information Found:

**May 31, 2023:** Oricon News reported that all 105 published volumes of One Piece had surpassed **1 million cumulative sales** each, making it the first manga series to achieve this milestone.

**September 10, 2021:** Volume 100 became #1 in comic rankings, and all 100 published volumes at that time had each sold over 1 million copies.

## Limitations in Findings:

Unfortunately, the Wikipedia sources I accessed do not contain the specific 2023-2024 data you're looking for, such as:
- Updated total circulation beyond 516.6 million
- Volume 106 or later specific sales figures
- Late 2023 or 2024 milestone announcements
- Recent Oricon sales reports for those periods

## Recommendation:

The most concrete recent data I found is the **May 31, 2023 Oricon News report** about all 105 volumes selling over 1 million copies each. For the more specific 2023-2024 sales figures and circulation updates you're seeking, you would likely need to access:

1. Recent Oricon sales reports directly
2. Shueisha press releases from 2023-2024
3. Anime News Network archives from those specific periods
4. Japanese news sources that report on manga sales milestones

The Wikipedia articles I found appear to be updated more slowly and may not include the very latest 2024 sales data you're looking for.

In a rare event due to the closeness of the two magazines' founding dates, *Weekly Shōnen Sunday* and *Weekly Shōnen Magazine* released a special combined issue on March 19, 2008.[5] In addition, other commemorative events, merchandise, and manga crossovers were planned for the following year as part of the celebrations.[4] The book *Shonen Sunday 1983* was published on July 15, 2009 to celebrate the anniversary and the magazine's heyday. Based on my comprehensive research using available Wikipedia sources, here's what I can tell you about Detective Conan's recent manga sales and circulation status:

## Current Official Circulation Figure
The **most recent official circulation number I could verify is 270 million copies worldwide**, as reported by Anime News Network on **January 22, 2023**. This milestone was announced around the release of the 26th movie "Black Iron Submarine."

## 2023-2024 Developments
While I found extensive information about Detective Conan's activities in 2023-2024, I couldn't locate any newer circulation announcements beyond the 270 million figure. Here's what's been happening:

### 2023 Highlights:
- **April 14, 2023**: "Black Iron Submarine" movie released and became the first film in the franchise to break ¥10 billion (approx. $106 million) at the Japanese box office
- The manga continued serialization in Weekly Shōnen Sunday
- Volume 104 was released in October 2023

### 2024 Developments:
- **April 2024**: New film "The Million-dollar Pentagram" released (though detailed box office data wasn't available in my search)
- Ongoing manga serialization

## Sales Context & Milestones
For perspective on Detective Conan's sales trajectory:
- **200 million copies**: Reached by April 2017
- **250 million copies**: Announced October 2021 (celebrating the 100th volume)
- **270 million copies**: January 2023

## Limitations & Recommendations
The search tools I had access to appear to have limited coverage of very recent news and press releases. For the most up-to-date circulation numbers, I recommend checking:

1. **Primary Sources**: Shogakukan's official announcements, Weekly Shōnen Sunday
2. **Recent Volume Releases**: New manga volume announcements typically include updated circulation figures
3. **Industry News**: Anime News Network, Crunchyroll News, Japanese sources like Natalie and Oricon News

**Bottom Line**: As of my research cutoff, 270 million copies worldwide remains the latest officially verified circulation figure for Detective Conan, announced in January 2023. The franchise continues to perform exceptionally well with blockbuster films and ongoing manga serialization, but any circulation updates beyond 270 million would likely come from official announcements tied to future volume releases or special events.

5. **Completed series like Demon Slayer** maintain huge cultural impact

The data suggests action/battle shonen remains the most commercially successful genre, with darker, more mature themes (like Chainsaw Man and Jujutsu Kaisen) gaining particular popularity among diverse age groups.

This list only includes the number of collected *tankōbon* volumes sold. For sales of manga magazines which includes these series, see *List of Japanese manga magazines by circulation*. After *Haeniwa no Zigzag* failed to be a serialized series, Tatsuhiko Katayama (Gotouge's first editor) suggested to start a series with an "easy-to-understand theme".[6] Gotouge's debut work *Kagarigari* would serve as a basis for *Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba*.[6] The series was published in *Weekly Shōnen Jump* from February 15, 2016, to May 18, 2020.[7][8] It became a success, with over 150 million copies in circulation (including digital copies) as of February 2021, making it one of the best-selling manga series of all time.[9][10]


In February 2021, Gotouge commented that their next project would be a science fiction romantic comedy story.[11]

[edit]

Gotouge has mentioned Hirohiko Araki's *JoJo's Bizarre Adventure;* Masashi Kishimoto's *Naruto;* Tite Kubo's *Bleach;* and Hideaki Sorachi's *Gintama* as influences on their work.[12][13][14]

After *Haeniwa no Zigzag* failed to be a serialized series, Tatsuhiko Katayama (Gotouge's first editor) suggested to start a series with an "easy-to-understand theme".[6] Gotouge's debut work *Kagarigari* would serve as a basis for *Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba*.[6] The series was published in *Weekly Shōnen Jump* from February 15, 2016, to May 18, 2020.[7][8] It became a success, with over 150 million copies in circulation (including digital copies) as of February 2021, making it one of the best-selling manga series of all time.[9][10]


In February 2021, Gotouge commented that their next project would be a science fiction romantic comedy story.[11]



## Influences

[edit]

Gotouge has mentioned Hirohiko Araki's *JoJo's Bizarre Adventure;* Masashi Kishimoto's *Naruto;* Tite Kubo's *Bleach;* and Hideaki Sorachi's *Gintama* as influences on their work.[12][13][14]

根据我搜索到的最新信息，以下是2023年表现最突出的几部日本漫画作品的数据：

## 2023年最热门的日本漫画作品

### 1. **Blue Lock** - 2023年最大爆款
- **销量表现**：曾是2023年上半年最佳销量漫画，在2022年11月至2023年5月期间销量超过**800万册**
- **总销量**：截至2023年8月，累计销量突破**2800万册**
- **增长速度**：从2022年12月的1600万册快速增长到2023年8月的2800万册，展现了爆炸性增长

### 2. **One Piece** - 持续霸主
- **2023年上半年表现**：单卷（第105卷）销量达到**176万册**
- **总销量**：继续保持全球漫画销量冠军地位
- **稳定性**：作为常青树，One Piece在2023年依然保持着强劲的销售表现

### 3. **Chainsaw Man** - 稳步上升
